newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ISPAT IPO BILLED AS STEEL INDUSTRY'S BIGGEST.
newsitem.headline: ISPAT IPO BILLED AS STEEL INDUSTRY'S BIGGEST.

text.p: The upcoming flotation of steel group Ispat International NV will be the largest initial public offering in the steel sector for at least 30 years, joint global coordinator CSFB said on Wednesday.
Ispat plans to float 19.25 million of its shares -- about 15 percent of the company -- at $22 to $26 each in Amsterdam and New York next month, raising net proceeds of some $360 million.

Ispat's chairman Lakshmi Mittal will retain 85 percent of the shares and 97.5 percent of the voting rights. At a news conference on Wednesday he declined to say whether he planned to sell off more shares in the future.
Indian-born Mittal is one of Britain's wealthiest men and has specialised in turning around loss-making steel firms.

Incorporated in the Netherlands, Ispat makes steel in Canada, Ireland, Germany, Mexico and the Caribbean, utilising an "integrated mini-mill process" which it says makes it one of the world's lowest cost steel producers.
In an issue prospectus Ispat said it would use the proceeds to repay $90 million of debt and to finance further growth.
Last month Ispat signed an agreement to acquire two units of Germany's Thyssen Stahl AG -- Stahl Ruhrort GmbH and Walzdraht Hochfeld GmbH.
And in Venezuela Ispat is among 11 pre-qualified bidders for the government-owned Sidor steel plant.
Mittal told reporters Ispat also saw various expansion opportunities in Asia and the U.S.
The Ispat group produces a broad range of semifinished and finished steel products for both the flat and long product markets, and has customers in over 60 countries.
It shipped six million tonnes of steel in 1996, and expects to ship some 10 million tonnes by 1999.
Based on the indicative price for the IPO, Mittal said Ispat's market capitalisation would be roughly one and a half times that of Dutch steel group Hoogovens NV .
He said the group's direct reduced iron (DRI) technology enabled it to produce steel more cheaply than other mini-mills and producers who use traditional blast-furnaces.
According to International Accounting Standards (IAS), Ispat posted a net profit of $613 million in 1996 on sales of net $1.77 billion. It plans to continue reporting according to IAS.
Under U.S. GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles), net income amounted to $336 million in 1996.
In the first half of 1997 sales came to $995 million while operating income plus depreciation (EBITDA) according to IAS amounted to $168 million versus $309 million in all of 1996.
Ispat CFO Bhikam Agarwal told reporters the company expected its EBITDA margin to rise from 16.9 percent in the first half of this to year to 21 or 22 percent in 1999.
The underwriters to Ispat's IPO have an option to place an extra 2.89 million shares with investors if the issue is oversubscribed.
